principles: A word that costs someone money

world_behind.title: The objection is financial
world_behind.text: Verse 3 says the popular part of the Zoramites was angry because the preaching destroyed their craft. Mormon puts the motive in one clause and does not elaborate.

world_behind.title: The leaders polled the people secretly
world_behind.text: Verse 5 says the rulers, priests, and teachers hid their own intentions and found out the minds of the people privily. The expulsion in verse 6 follows a covert survey.

world_behind.title: Everyone who agreed was expelled
world_behind.text: Verse 6 says they were many. The poor of Alma 32 were shut out of buildings; now anyone persuaded is put out of the country.

world_behind.title: The people of Ammon are threatened for taking them in
world_behind.text: Verses 8 and 9 have the Zoramite chief ruler demand they be cast out, and breathe out threatenings. The people of Ammon refuse and receive the refugees anyway.

world_behind.title: They give land, not only shelter
world_behind.text: Verse 9 lists nourishing, clothing, lands for inheritance, and ministering according to their wants. Alma 27 had them receiving exactly this from the Nephites.

world_behind.title: Jershon is vacated for an army
world_behind.text: Verse 13 has the people of Ammon move to Melek so the land can become a staging ground. They give up an inheritance to keep the covenant of Alma 24 intact.

world_behind.title: The converts take up arms
world_behind.text: Verse 14 says the Zoramites brought to repentance now defend themselves, their wives, children, and lands. Their neighbors in Jershon had buried their weapons.

words.text: A trade, and the income from it. The record uses the word twice and the King James Bible six times; Acts 19:25 has a silversmith telling his guild that by this craft they have their wealth, just before a riot against Paul. Mormon uses it for the same kind of objection.

Secretly, without being noticed. Treated at Alma 14:3. It appears four times in the record, and the King James Bible fifteen. Here the leaders learn the people's minds without letting the people learn theirs, which turns a consultation into an intelligence operation.

Threats, stated to intimidate. Treated at Mosiah 19:3. The record uses it ten times and the King James Bible twice, one of which is Saul breathing out threatenings against the disciples. Mormon uses the same verb, and the people of Ammon are unmoved by it.

Between. The word turns up five times here, and the King James Bible sixteen. Mormon uses it to date the start of the war in the eighteenth year, and to say that the fighting begins in the land the people of Ammon just vacated.

Rigor, exactness in requirement. The word occurs twice in this record and never in the King James Bible. Jacob 2 has hearts pierced by the strictness of the word; here people are offended by it, and Mormon names it as what turned them hard.

An instruction laid on someone as a duty. Treated at 2 Nephi 20:6. Its count is ten times in this book, while the King James Bible a hundred and two. Benjamin gave Mosiah charge over the kingdom; Alma gives each son his own, separately, and Alma 36 through 42 are the text of them.

phrases.term: They were angry because of the word, for it did destroy their craft
phrases.text: Mormon supplies the motive before the response. The preaching threatened a livelihood, and the anger that follows is presented as an economic reaction dressed as a religious one.

phrases.term: Their rulers and their priests and their teachers did not let the people know concerning their desires
phrases.text: The leadership consults while concealing its own position. Mormon notes the asymmetry, and verse 6 shows what it was for: identifying who to expel.

phrases.term: Those who were in favor of the words which had been spoken by Alma and his brethren were cast out of the land; and they were many
phrases.text: The last clause is the sting. The mission worked, and the measure of its success is the size of the refugee column moving toward Jershon.

phrases.term: He breathed out many threatenings against them
phrases.text: The Zoramite ruler's demand, in language the King James Bible uses of Saul before Damascus. Mormon reports the threat and the refusal in the same verse.

phrases.term: They did receive all the poor of the Zoramites that came over unto them
phrases.text: The people of Ammon take in a whole displaced population under threat of war. Alma 27 had them arriving in Jershon as refugees themselves, and Mormon lets the reader make the connection.

phrases.term: They did nourish them, and did clothe them, and did give unto them lands for their inheritance
phrases.text: Three verbs and a grant of property. The clothing is pointed: Alma 32 said these people were excluded over the coarseness of their apparel.

phrases.term: Gave place in the land of Jershon for the armies of the Nephites
phrases.text: The people of Ammon hand over the land they were granted so it can become a battlefield. Their covenant keeps them out of the fighting, so they move instead of staying to be defended in place.

phrases.term: They have taken up arms to defend themselves, and their wives, and children, and their lands
phrases.text: The Zoramite converts make the opposite decision from their hosts. Mormon records both choices without ranking them, and the two peoples live in the same story.

phrases.term: They began to be offended because of the strictness of the word
phrases.text: Alma's grief in Zarahemla has a stated cause. The word had not softened and the people had, and Mormon says the offense was at the strictness itself.

phrases.term: That he might give unto them every one his charge, separately
phrases.text: Alma gathers three sons and speaks to each alone. The separateness is recorded deliberately, and the next seven chapters are what he said.

verses.label: v. 1–2
verses.title: One place name carries a third of its scriptural uses
verses.text: "The land of Jershon" stands at verses 1, 2, 6, 13 and 14, and scripture has the phrase fifteen times in all. Both opening verses end by arriving there: first Amulek and those with him, then "the rest of the brethren." Before the chapter has a conflict it has a destination, and everyone in it is either going to Jershon or being sent away from somewhere else.

verses.label: v. 4–6
verses.title: An assembly is called and no decision comes out of it
verses.text: The Zoramites "sent and gathered together throughout all the land all the people, and consulted with them" — the shape of a public meeting, with the leaders' own aim withheld from the room. What the process produces is not a verdict but a roll: "those who were in favor of the words which had been spoken by Alma and his brethren were cast out of the land; and they were many." The record gives the machinery of consultation being used to take a census of dissent.

verses.label: v. 9
verses.title: A threat is answered with an inventory
verses.text: Against the Zoramite ruler's demand, the people of Ammon "did not fear their words," and what follows is four verbs rather than an argument: they nourished them, clothed them, gave them lands for their inheritance, and administered to them "according to their wants." The record declines to report anything the people of Ammon said in reply.

verses.label: v. 13
verses.title: The people who will not fight move house for a battlefield
verses.text: They depart Jershon and "gave place in the land of Jershon for the armies of the Nephites." That phrase appears three times in scripture, the others at Judges 20:36 and Galatians 2:5. Their pacifism costs them the land they were given in Alma 27, and the record states the transaction without comment before closing the year.

verses.label: v. 14
verses.title: The verbs change tense inside the verse
verses.text: The converts "were brought to repentance" and "were driven out of their land," and then the sentence moves to the present: "they have lands for their inheritance in the land of Jershon, and they have taken up arms to defend themselves." The record does not say whose present that is, and the ground in question was vacated one verse earlier.

verses.label: v. 15–16
verses.title: The war chapter ends by naming a document
verses.text: Alma's grief is given as the cause of what comes next: "Therefore, he caused that his sons should be gathered together, that he might give unto them every one his charge, separately." Then the source: "we have an account of his commandments, which he gave unto them according to his own record," a phrase used at Alma 5:2 and nowhere else in scripture. Seven chapters of counsel follow, and the record has told the reader where they came from before it prints a word of them.

chapter.title: The mission succeeded and produced a refugee crisis
chapter.text: Verse 6 puts both facts together: those "in favor of the words which had been spoken by Alma and his brethren were cast out of the land; and they were many." The count and the eviction share a clause. Verse 9 then reports the receiving side, the people of Ammon, who "did receive all the poor of the Zoramites that came over unto them," and Alma 43:4 records the military consequence, that "the Zoramites became Lamanites" and marched on Jershon.

chapter.title: Money is named as the reason for the anger
chapter.text: Verse 3 says the word destroyed their craft. Everything the Zoramites do afterward follows from a threat to income, and the record says so plainly.

chapter.title: The consultation was a screening
chapter.text: Verse 4 describes a general assembly, "they sent and gathered together throughout all the land all the people, and consulted with them." Verse 5 supplies what the leaders withheld, "their rulers and their priests and their teachers did not let the people know concerning their desires; therefore they found out privily the minds of all the people." Verse 6 gives the outcome. The record thus reports a consultation whose purpose was identification, and the sequence, gather, conceal, sort, expel, occupies three verses.

chapter.title: Refugees receive refugees
chapter.text: The people of Ammon had arrived in Jershon with nothing eleven years earlier. They now give land, clothing, and food to a second displaced people, under threat.

chapter.title: They give up the land rather than the covenant
chapter.text: Jershon was granted to them and they hand it back so an army can use it. The cost of keeping their oath in Alma 24 is paid here in property.

chapter.title: Two converted peoples make opposite choices about arms
chapter.text: The people of Ammon will not fight; the Zoramite converts take up arms for their families and lands. Mormon puts both in one chapter and passes no judgment.

chapter.title: Offense at strictness is the diagnosis for Zarahemla
chapter.text: Alma's sorrow is not about a foreign nation. His own people are hardening, and what they object to is the exactness of what he has been preaching.

chapter.title: The chapter ends by turning private
chapter.text: After war preparations and national movements, Mormon closes on a father gathering three sons and speaking to each alone. The next seven chapters are that conversation.

applications.title: Watch what a message costs the people who take it
applications.text: The Zoramite leaders were angry "because it did destroy their craft," and those who agreed with the preaching "were cast out of the land; and they were many." Before you press an argument, know what it will cost the person who accepts it.

applications.title: Notice a consultation designed to identify people
applications.text: The leaders gathered everyone and asked their minds, having first concealed their own, "therefore they found out privily the minds of all the people." A process that looks participatory can be an instrument for sorting. Ask what will be done with the answers.

applications.title: Receive the people the decision displaced
applications.text: The people of Ammon "did receive all the poor of the Zoramites that came over unto them; and they did nourish them, and did clothe them, and did give unto them lands for their inheritance." Four verbs and all of them material.

applications.title: Refuse the demand to hand people over
applications.text: The Zoramite ruler asked that the refugees be cast out and "breathed out many threatenings against them." The record says simply that "the people of Ammon did not fear their words; therefore they did not cast them out."

applications.title: Expect the generosity to have a bill
applications.text: Sheltering the refugees moved the people of Ammon out of Jershon and brought the Nephite armies in, and Alma 43 opens with the war that followed. Doing the right thing here has a stated, traceable cost in the next chapter.

applications.title: Say what your work produced without exaggerating it
applications.text: The summary is careful, "as many as were brought to repentance were driven out of their land." The result is stated with its consequence attached, and neither half is dropped.

applications.title: Report the grief rather than the argument
applications.text: Alma's sorrow is given a cause and it is not the opposition, "because of the iniquity of the people." The chapter has him distressed about what people are doing to themselves rather than about what they did to him.

applications.title: Answer a family problem with a conversation
applications.text: The chapter ends with Alma gathering his sons "that he might give unto them every one his charge, separately," which is what Alma 36 through 42 consists of. Sorrow about a whole people is answered by three individual conversations.

questions.text: What would I lose if the thing I resist turned out to be true?
When have I asked for input while hiding what I had already decided?
What has agreeing with something true cost me?
Who has arrived in my life needing something, and what did I actually give?
What would I hand over to keep a promise I made?
Where have I been offended by the strictness of something rather than its truth?
Who needs to hear from me alone, and about what?
